message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Test
on:
  - push
  - pull_request

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-v: [20.x, 22.x, 24.x]
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v2
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}

      - name: Fetch submodules
        run: git submodule update --init

      - name: Cache npm dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.npm
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-node-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-node-

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run test suite
        run: npm run test",
  "rationale": "The repository runs npm ci on every push/pull_request across a three-cell matrix and ships a committed package-lock.json, so dependency fetching is repeated and the lockfile can serve as a cache input. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (dependency_cache mechanism) is evidence-supported (reported vm_time_reduction: free 6%, paid 3.4%) and its preconditions are met: repeated dependency fetching is measurable and cache inputs include the lockfile. No equivalent cache already exists. Adding actions/cache@v4 for ~/.npm keyed on package-lock.json before npm ci speeds installs without removing or altering any build/test step, so intended coverage is preserved. No permissions are weakened, no privileged actions or secrets are added, and no new network access is introduced beyond the existing npm registry use.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
